long:
Start the local Dashboard server in the foreground; Ctrl-C stops it.

It listens on 127.0.0.1 only and opens your browser on a session URL. The proof in
that URL works once: the first page or client that opens it gets the run's only
session, with the same access as your gh login on this machine, and the terminal
prints "session opened". Keep the URL private until then; restart for a new one.
--no-browser prints the session URL instead of opening a browser.

The page is the Dashboard UI built from dashboard/; a binary built without it serves
a placeholder page. The API is under /api/.

flags.name: port
flags.usage: port to listen on (default: any free port)

short: Set up Nibfin in a repository
long:
Set up Nibfin in a repository and open one PR that imports its workflows.

It sets the labels request, scope, shaped, delivered, pause and pending; pull request
creation limited to collaborators; approval required for fork PR workflows (all
external contributors on a public repository, "Require approval for fork pull
request workflows" on a private one); "Automatically delete head branches" off; only
rebase merge allowed; "Require branches to be up to date before merging" off in
the repository rulesets and the branch protection on the default branch, with
every other rule kept (it creates none, and lists inherited organization or
enterprise rulesets as a note with their link); the
variable NIBFIN_EXECUTION_REPO; and the Secret NIBFIN_GITHUB_TOKEN from the current
gh login, which needs the workflow scope (gh auth refresh -s workflow). It neither
writes nor reads NIBFIN_PROVIDER: each Runner names its provider in its .env.

The PR on branch nibfin/init holds the execution set when this host's Runners serve
the repository, the peer set otherwise. Without Runners it stops and points to
gh nibfin runner add. For the peer set the gh login must be admin of the Runners'
repository too; otherwise init stops before any write. An initialized repository
gets no PR; use gh nibfin upgrade.

The workflow files are rendered by nibfin render-workflows in the latest attested
Nibfin image, run with this host's Podman; they pin that image by digest and call
nibfin-core's Action at the commit the image was built from.

GitHub offers Issues "Creation allowed by: Collaborators only" only in the web UI;
init prints the Settings link to set it there.

flags.name: repo
flags.usage: target repository as [HOST/]OWNER/REPO (default: the current directory's repository)

short: Log in to a provider for the Runners

long:
Pause Nibfin work on Issues.

An issue is a number (N or #N) in the -R repository, or an Issue URL.
Several issues can be given at once; there is no confirmation step.

flags.name: repo
flags.usage: target repository as [HOST/]OWNER/REPO (default: the current directory's repository)

long:
Resume Nibfin work on Issues.

An issue is a number (N or #N) in the -R repository, or an Issue URL.
Several issues can be given at once; there is no confirmation step.

On one pending Issue whose repair record waits for a choice (gh nibfin status
shows its options, which are suggestions), it first writes the decision, then
removes pause and pending, and reads both back:
  --option N      writes the marked decision comment for option N.
  --reply TEXT    posts TEXT, trimmed, as one ordinary comment without a marker;
                  Nibfin's next Shape run takes it as written. For a long reply
                  use the shell, for example --reply "$(cat reply.md)".
Use one of them, not both.

flags.name: option
flags.usage: answer the repair record's options with option N (one Issue)

flags.name: reply
flags.usage: answer the repair record in your own words; posted as written (one Issue)

short: Add Runners for a provider on this host
long:
Add Runners for a provider on this host (the Linux host, or the podman machine VM).

The first Runner on the host registers to the current directory's repository; later
Runners reuse the repository the existing Runners use. Each Runner carries the label
nibfin-<user id> (and nibfin when you are admin of the repository), names its provider
as NIBFIN_PROVIDER in its .env, and runs as a systemd user service.

A Runner's .env may also set NIBFIN_MODEL=<model> for that Runner only; without it,
Core's default for the provider applies. runner add does not write that line, and
runner add and upgrade keep it. Restart the Runner after changing its .env. An old
NIBFIN_MODEL repository variable is unused and can be deleted.

An admin registers directly. A collaborator with write access gets the registration
token through a "Nibfin runner request" Issue, encrypted to an SSH key of their GitHub
account that is in ~/.ssh; the command waits up to 10 minutes for the answer. On a
private repository the request also carries a read-only deploy key, created once per
repository at ~/.local/share/nibfin/deploy-keys/<host>/<owner>/<name>/id_ed25519
(under XDG_DATA_HOME when set); the owner removes the deploy key nibfin-runner-<login>
under Settings > Deploy keys together with your Runners.

A collaborator's Runners get a job-started hook in ~/.local/share/nibfin/hook (under
XDG_DATA_HOME when set), so they run only official Nibfin Jobs for you. The hook checks
that nibfin-shared-runner.yml started the Job for your user id, that it and
nibfin-job.yml at that commit match the official files except the image digest and
the nibfin-core Action commit, that the image's Sigstore signature and signer
(nibfin-core's image.yml on main) verify on the host, and that the Action commit is
the commit the image was built from. runner add renders the official files with
nibfin render-workflows in the latest attested image on this host's Podman. A
refused Job fails before any step, with the reason under "Set up
runner" in its log. A private repository is read with the deploy key and needs git and
ssh on the runner host. Each Job reads the attestation API without a credential (60
requests per hour per IP). After the owner upgrades the repository, run runner add
again; after Sigstore's root changes, update gh-nibfin and run runner add again.

flags.name: yes
flags.usage: apply the plan without asking to confirm

short: Remove Runners for a provider on this host
long:
Remove Runners for a provider on this host (the Linux host, or the podman machine VM).

Without --count every Runner of the provider is removed. Idle Runners go first. A busy
Runner loses its nibfin labels, so it takes no new nibfin Job, and its GitHub registration
is deleted once its Job ends; the command waits for it and never cancels the Job. Each
removal deletes the GitHub registration, then the service and the Runner's directory. A
count above the number of Runners is refused.

One Runner's failure does not stop the others, and the remaining Runners are read back
even after a failure. A Runner that GitHub reports offline while its Job still runs fails
alone: run runner remove again once it is back or its Job is resolved.

When you are not admin of the Runners' repository (a collaborator's Runners), the removal
is local: it waits for a running Job, then deletes the service and the directory only.
The GitHub registration stays; the repository's owner deletes it under Settings → Actions →
Runners, and GitHub removes a runner offline for more than 14 days.

When the host's last Runner of any provider goes, the job-started hook of a
collaborator's Runners goes with it.

--delete-login deletes the provider's login (the nibfin-home-<provider> volume) only
when no Runner of the provider remains on this host.

flags.name: delete-login
flags.usage: also delete the provider login when no Runner of it remains

short: Show the runner host, logins and the Issues Nibfin works on
long:
Show the runner host, logins and the Issues Nibfin works on. It only reads.

Always: the podman machine and its free memory, each Runner's service against
GitHub's online/busy, and each provider's login.

Without -R (the person view): your open scope or request Issues across
repositories, with pause/pending, the pending comment and whether each repository
uses the latest image.
With -R (the repository view): all open Issues of that repository, its image and
whether a Nibfin run succeeded after the init PR merged.

flags.name: repo
flags.usage: show the repository view of [HOST/]OWNER/REPO (default: the person view)

long:
Upgrade Nibfin in a repository and bring this host's Runners to the current spec.

The repository part renders the workflows with nibfin render-workflows in the latest
attested image, run with this host's Podman (a stopped podman machine stops upgrade
before any write: start it and run upgrade again), and opens one PR on branch
nibfin/upgrade when they differ from the default branch.

The host part runs whether or not the workflows are current. Each configured
Runner on this host gets what runner add sets up today: NIBFIN_PROVIDER in its
.env (other lines, such as NIBFIN_MODEL, are kept), the current systemd user unit, enabled and active, and, when the gh login
is admin of the Runners' repository, the labels nibfin and nibfin-<user id>.
Without admin the labels are left as they are. Runners are changed one at a
time; a Runner running a Job is restarted only after the Job ends, so the
others keep taking work. A stopped podman machine is not started.
